facts.fact: The timeline mechanism is async/await over Promise-wrapped setTimeout — NOT requestAnimationFrame, NOT CSS keyframe tracks, NOT a custom scheduler. JS decides WHEN to toggle classes; CSS transitions perform the motion.

facts.fact: Scenes loop forever via for(;;) with d.init(stage) resetting DOM to frame zero each iteration; cancellation uses an abort token whose rejected promise (Symbol ABORT) unwinds the async stack at the next await.

## CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF'S PREMISE — READ FIRST

**"The app UI is FRENCH" is false as a blanket statement.** The app is **bilingual by surface**, and the split is sharp and consistent:

| Surface | Language | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **WhatsApp inbox** (`src/whatsapp/`) | **100% French** | Every label, placeholder, tooltip, menu item: "Toutes", "Non lues", "Entrez un message", "Nouvelle discussion" |
| **Admin dashboard** (`src/pages/admin/*`, `src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`) | **English chrome, French destructive/edge copy** | Nav = `Dashboard`, `Orders`, `Delivery Services`, `Webhooks`. But `ConfirmDialog`s and error toasts are French |
| **Courier sidebar** (`CourierSidebar.tsx:24-26`) | **French** | `Tableau de bord`, `Commandes`, `Paiements` |
| **Media-buyer sidebar** (`MediaBuyerSidebar.tsx:47-63`) | **French** | `Tableau de bord`, `Statistiques`, `Publicités` → `Campagnes globales`, `Publicités produits`, `Commandes`, `Paiements`, `Demandes` |
| **Seller sidebar** (`SellerSidebar.tsx:35-49`) | **English** | `Dashboard`, `My wallet`, `Delivery notes` |

**Demo implication:** a demo that renders the admin Webhooks page in French would be inventing copy. The WhatsApp inbox demo, conversely, must be entirely French. Do not "translate for consistency" — the inconsistency is the product.

## 1. WHATSAPP INBOX — `src/whatsapp/routes/admin/Conversations.tsx` (864 L) + `conversations/parts.tsx` (11,252 L)

**This is a deliberate WhatsApp Web pixel-replica in DARK mode.** File header, `Conversations.tsx:3-9`:
> "WhatsApp Web pixel-replica in dark/refresh mode… Three panes: chat list ← chat pane ← info pane"

It **breaks the app's light theme entirely.** Everything else is cream `#faf9f5`; this is `#0A0A0A`.

### Files
- Route wrapper: `src/whatsapp/WhatsappConversations.tsx` → `/whatsapp/conversations`
- Orchestrator: `src/whatsapp/routes/admin/Conversations.tsx`
- **All UI**: `src/whatsapp/routes/admin/conversations/parts.tsx` — `ChatList` (L270), `ChatRow` (L845), `FilterChipRow` (L1135), `ChatPane` (L2857), `Bubble` (L4831), `InfoPane` (L9570), `EmptyState` (L2531), `ConnectionGate` (L2659)
- CSS: `src/whatsapp/routes/admin/conversations/conversations.css`
- Seller variant: `src/whatsapp/WhatsappSellerInbox.tsx` → `/seller/whatsapp`

### Layout (`conversations.css:77-115`)
```css
.wac { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 400px 1fr; border-radius: 18px; height:100%; }
.wac.is-with-info { grid-template-columns: 400px 1fr 400px; }
font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, …;  font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.4;
```
Page is flushed to `height: calc(100vh - 28px)` to match the sidebar pill's geometry (`:root[data-route="conversations"] .layout__main`). Info pane is **hidden by default**, toggled by clicking the chat header.

### Tokens (`conversations.css:24-77`) — the whole design intent is in the comment
> "ALL chrome surfaces share one black (#0A0A0A)… The only places that lift off that base are elements that must be visibly elevated: the input/search pills, message bubbles, and row hover/active states."

--wa-bubble-out: #264C39   --wa-bubble-out-deep: #1E3D2E   --wa-bubble-in: #1F1F1F

--wa-text-primary: #E9EDEF   --wa-text-secondary: #8696A0   --wa-text-tertiary: #6B7C85
--wa-text-link: #53BDEB   --wa-border: #262626
--wa-green: #00A884   --wa-blue-tick: #53BDEB   --wa-danger: #F15C6D
--wa-r-bubble: 7.5px   --wa-r-pill: 21px   --wa-r-lg: 8px   --wa-r-md: 6px

### THE BATCH PATH (commit `e81b63c`, `DeliveryNoteWizard.tsx:248-736`)
```js
const BATCH_MAX = 100;
export function providerSupportsBatch(provider) {
    const t = String(provider?.provider_type || '').toLowerCase();
    if (t.includes('coliaty')) return true;
    if (t.includes('digylog')) return true;
    if (t.includes('vitex')) {
        return !(provider?.vitex_parcel_fragile === true || provider?.vitex_parcel_open === true);
    }
    return false;
}
```
**Only Coliaty (`/parcel/normal/mass`), Digylog (`/orders`), and Vitex (`/add-parcels`) batch.** Vitex is public-path only — fragile/forbid-open force the per-parcel dashboard flow. Trigger is `orders.length > 1 && providerSupportsBatch(provider)`; everything else keeps the per-parcel path. **Batch is invisible in the UI** — same `creating` spinner, same review list. Live-verified on a 200-parcel Coliaty run (2×100).

recon.findings:
## DEFINITIVE ALLOW/DENY LIST — WhatsApp Cloud API (verified against Meta docs, July 2026)

Four findings overturn common assumptions and should be read first: **typing indicators ARE supported**, **Groups ARE supported (but capped at 8 participants)**, **message history backfill IS possible (Coexistence only, 180 days)**, and **edit/delete are NOT available to the business in any form**. The unofficial-library implementation almost certainly relies on capabilities in the DENY column, so the marketing site must be built from this list, not from the existing product.

---

### 1. Inbound messages via webhooks — SUPPORTED (with a carve-out)
Text, image, video, audio, document, location, contacts, sticker, and reaction all arrive via the `messages` webhook. Payloads up to 3 MB. The contacts object carries only `profile.name` and `wa_id`.
`https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages` · `https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/webhooks/payload-examples/`

**Carve-out:** anything Cloud API cannot parse arrives as an `unsupported` webhook with error `131051` ("Message type is currently not supported"). The documented unsupported enum is verbatim: `button, edit, errors, gif, group_invite, hsm, image, interactive, keep_in_chat, link_preview, list, location, media_placeholder, order, pin, poll_creation, poll_update, product, reaction`. Note this list is context-dependent (image/location/reaction appear in it despite being supported types generally) — do not read it as a flat blocklist.
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/webhooks/reference/messages/unsupported/`

### 2. Free-form text + the 24-hour window — SUPPORTED inside, HARD DENY outside
Verbatim: *"When a WhatsApp user messages you or calls you, a 24-hour timer called a customer service window starts."* It **resets** to a full 24h on each new user message or call. Inside: any message type, no pre-approval, **free**. Outside, verbatim: *"When the window closes, you can only send pre-approved template messages."* — this is the single most important constraint on the site's messaging.

Additional: opt-in is mandatory — messaging is restricted to users who *"have opted in to receiving messages from you."* Free Entry Point (Click-to-WhatsApp ad / Page CTA): responding within 24h opens a **72-hour** window in which all messages are free.
`https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages`

### 3. Templates — SUPPORTED, approval mandatory
Verbatim: *"Each template must be categorized as authentication, marketing, or utility."* and *"Templates are automatically reviewed upon creation or after editing."* Status → `APPROVED` before sending. Verbatim: *"Template messages are the only type of message that can be sent to WhatsApp users outside of a customer service window."*
`https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/overview`

**Pricing (changed — do not market the old model):** per-message since **July 1, 2025**; conversation-based pricing is deprecated. Charged only on **delivery**. Marketing = always charged. Utility = **free inside an open service window**, charged outside. Authentication = charged outside windows. All non-template service messages inside a window = free.
`https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing`

### 4. Read receipts — SUPPORTED
`POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/messages` with `{"messaging_product":"whatsapp","status":"read","message_id":"<WAMID>"}`. Produces the two blue checks.
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/typing-indicators/`

### 5. Typing indicators — SUPPORTED, CONDITIONAL (demoable with constraints)
**This is legal to demo.** Verbatim payload:
```json
{
  "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
  "status": "read",
  "message_id": "<WHATSAPP_MESSAGE_ID>",
  "typing_indicator": { "type": "text" }
}
```
Three hard constraints the demo must respect: (a) it is **bundled with the read receipt** — the same call marks the message read, so you cannot show typing without also showing blue ticks; (b) it **requires an inbound `message_id`** — you can never show typing spontaneously or outside a reply context; (c) verbatim: *"The typing indicator will be dismissed once you respond, or after 25 seconds, whichever comes first."* Policy note: *"only display a typing indicator if you are going to respond."*
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/typing-indicators/`

### 6. Customer online / last-seen presence — NOT SUPPORTED
No endpoint or webhook exists. Inbound webhooks expose only `profile.name` and `wa_id`. There is no presence surface in the Cloud API doc index (Messaging, Calling, Groups, Webhooks, Templates, Analytics, Phone Number Management).
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/` · `https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/webhooks/payload-examples/`

### 7. Reactions — SUPPORTED (send and receive)
`"type":"reaction"` with `reaction.message_id` + `reaction.emoji` (Unicode). Inbound reactions arrive via the reaction webhook.
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/messages/reaction-messages/` · `https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/reaction/`

### 8. Editing a sent message — NOT SUPPORTED (deny outright)
There is **no business-side edit API**. The only edit surface is an inbound webhook fired when *"A WhatsApp user edits a previously sent message"* (15-min user limit), and it is doubly gated: verbatim *"The edit webhook is only available to WhatsApp Business app users (aka 'Coexistence')"* AND currently broken — verbatim: *"Edit messages are temporarily unsupported. Edited messages are currently delivered as an unsupported message type webhook instead of an edit webhook."* Groups docs independently confirm businesses cannot edit messages.
`https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/edit/`

### 9. Deleting / revoking a sent message — NOT SUPPORTED (deny outright)
Same shape as edit. No business-side revoke API. The revoke webhook fires only when *"A WhatsApp user revokes (deletes) a previously sent message"* (within 2 days), payload `"revoke": {"original_message_id": "..."}`, and is *"only available to WhatsApp Business app users (aka 'Coexistence')"*. Groups docs confirm businesses cannot delete messages.
`https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/revoke`

### 10. View-once — NOT SUPPORTED, both directions
Cannot send: view-once is explicitly in the Groups unsupported list, and no send schema exists on `/messages`. Cannot meaningfully receive: inbound view-once falls through to the `unsupported` webhook (error 131051). The existing product's view-once handling is a direct artifact of the unofficial library and **cannot be demoed**.
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/groups/` · `https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/webhooks/reference/messages/unsupported/`

### 11. Groups — SUPPORTED but severely CONDITIONAL (demo only with the caps stated)
Groups API is **generally available**: verbatim *"The Groups API is now open to all businesses with an Official Business Account (OBA)."* Send via `recipient_type: "group"` + group ID in `to`. Delivery/read webhooks fire.

The caps make most "group broadcast" marketing false:
- **`"Max group participants: 8"`** — verbatim. This is not a broadcast channel.
- `"Max groups you can create: 10,000 per business number"`
- **OBA required**: *"To qualify for groups features, your business must be an Official Business Account (OBA)."*
- **Invite-link only** — no direct member addition. Participants join via a link you send.
- Supported in groups: text, media, text-based and media-based templates.
- Unsupported in groups: *"Calling, Disappearing messages, View-once, Auth, Commerce messages, Interactive messages"*; also no edit/delete, no hidden participant lists.
- Not available for WhatsApp Business app numbers or Multi-solution Conversations numbers.
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/groups/` · `https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups`

### 12. Customer contact / profile-picture fetching — NOT SUPPORTED
Profile pictures exist only for the **business's own** profile (editable via Business Profiles endpoint). No API returns a customer's avatar. Inbound gives `profile.name` + `wa_id` only. Any UI showing customer avatars must use business-supplied data, not WhatsApp.
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/reference/business-profiles/`

### 13. Multi-agent shared inbox — PRODUCT-LAYER (safe to demo)
Not a Cloud API concept. No assignment, claim, or agent primitives exist in the API. Cloud API delivers webhooks to one endpoint; routing/assignment/agent state is entirely the vendor's own layer. **Safe to market** — it is your software, not a Meta feature. Do not describe it as a "WhatsApp feature."
`https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/`

### 14. Message history / backfill on connect — CONDITIONAL (Coexistence only)
Default Cloud API: **NOT SUPPORTED**. There is no read-back endpoint. Verbatim: *"Messages have a maximum retention period of 30 days in order to provide the base features and functionality of the Cloud API service; for example, retransmissions."* Meta deletes user identifiers within 30 days of last status update. Cloud API is a stream, not a store — the vendor must persist messages itself.

**Exception — Coexistence** (onboarding an existing WhatsApp Business app number via Embedded Signup): history sync covers *"all messages sent or received within 180 days of the time when the business was onboarded onto Cloud API"*, via the `history` webhook; `smb_message_echoes` streams messages sent from the Business app post-onboarding; contacts sync via `smb_app_state_sync`. Caveats: *"group chat messages will not be included"*, *"media messages will not include media asset IDs"*, and Coexistence numbers have *"a fixed throughput of 20 mps"*. Also confirmed: without Coexistence, migrating loses history.
`https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/data-privacy-and-security/` · `https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/onboarding-business-app-users`

### 15. Broadcast / bulk — CONDITIONAL (templates + opt-in + tiers). **Tier model changed Oct 7, 2025.**
No "broadcast" primitive; bulk = looping approved templates to opted-in users, subject to messaging limits.

**Messaging limits are now PORTFOLIO-scoped, not per-number** (effective **October 7, 2025**) — all numbers in a portfolio **share** one limit. Definition: *"maximum number of unique WhatsApp user phone numbers your business can deliver messages to, outside of a customer service window, within a moving 24-hour period."*
Tiers: **250** (new portfolios) → **2,000** → **10,000** → **100,000** → **Unlimited**.
Reaching 2,000 requires one of: verify your business directly; have a partner verify it; or send 2,000 delivered messages to unique numbers in 30 days with high-quality templates outside service windows. Above that, auto-scaling needs high-quality messages across all numbers/templates **and** *"in the last 7 days, your business has utilized at least half of your current messaging limit"* → limit rises one level **within 6 hours** (down from 24h).
Notably: the **"Flagged" state is no longer possible** and limits *"will not be downgraded"* on quality drops.

Throughput: **80 messages/sec** default per business number (upgradeable); **1 message per 6 seconds to the same user** (~10/min). Higher throughput now requires 100K+ unique contacts/24h, unlimited portfolio limit, and Medium+ quality.
**MM Lite API** is the optimized marketing path with features not on Cloud API.

## 2. Hermes — DOES NOT EXIST AS SOFTWARE. This is the headline finding.

Exhaustive search returned **exactly two prose mentions and zero implementation**:
- `docs/wa-mancer-recon/10-integration-blueprint.md:152` and `:182` — the only two lines in the entire repo. Verbatim (§13.5): *"Toolbox `.211` = **shared app-wide tools** (Reacher/email-check, IP-geo, Hermes AI) — **NOT** WhatsApp workers (different concern/lifecycle; Hermes may be heavy)."*
- `vps.env:25` comment.
- Memory `igrowfast-toolbox-vps.md:10`: *"Purpose: light services fleet — **Hermes AI agent (hosted-LLM orchestrator)**, Reacher email checker, Redis, future tools."* Same file, same paragraph (`:18`): *"**No app services deployed yet.**"*
- Memory `supabase-selfhost-install.md:22`: *"Read replica / Evolution / **Hermes = separate boxes, later**."*

Negative evidence, all clean: `grep -ril hermes` over the whole repo (excluding node_modules/dist/.git) → **1 file, a doc**. `grep -ril hermes ops/` → **nothing**. `find . -iname "*hermes*"` → **nothing**. `git log --all -S"Hermes" -i` → 3 commits, all of which only add/remove *documentation and agent-skill files*, never code.

**Answer to "what is a Hermes agent": it is an AI agent — a hosted-LLM orchestrator — and it is a NAME FOR A PLAN, not a running system.** It is not an email-sending thing (that is **Reacher**, a separate co-tenant on the same box, also unbuilt) and it is not a deployed worker. There is no schema, no table, no container, no env var, no config, no code path. There is no definition anywhere of what one "agent" *is* as a countable unit — no per-agent row, no per-agent cost, no LLM provider selected.

**Consequence for pricing: "metered on Hermes agents" is metering a unit that has no implementation, no cost basis, and no definition.** Its cost is 100% unknown because the LLM provider is unchosen — and hosted-LLM inference is the one cost in this whole stack that is genuinely *variable per use*, unlike every VPS line item. The memory's own hedge — "Hermes may be heavy" — is the only sizing statement that exists.

Tiers metered on WhatsApp numbers + Hermes agents. **Costs must be recon'd, not invented.**"*

**There is no cost data in this repo. None. Not one currency figure for infrastructure, WhatsApp numbers, or Hermes.** The only real prices in the system are the three live MAD plan rows (599 / 5999 / 30000) — the thing being replaced.

The true cost basis lives in **three billing dashboards the repo cannot see: Contabo (3 VPS), Cloudflare (R2 + Turnstile + Tunnels), Hostinger (mailbox)**, plus Verifalia credits. Pull those four invoices; everything else is fabrication.

And the two metering units the owner picked are the two weakest available: **Hermes agents do not exist** (no code, no cost, no definition, no LLM provider chosen), and **WhatsApp numbers have ~zero marginal cost today under Baileys but per-conversation Meta billing after the planned Cloud API cutover** — the metric inverts at the migration.
